conversation:
maya (product): hey team :wave: quick sync — CX asked for a clear upgrade/migration story for private deploys. they want minimal downtime and a network handshake flow that their netops can sign off on. can we outline constraints and shipable pieces for M1?

ben (infra): can you clarify which customers? big on-prem vs managed VPC? tradeoffs differ.

maya (product): mainly two customers: one full air-gapped on-prem (customer A) and one VPC with customer-managed transit / firewall rules (customer B). both need an operator-friendly path and rollback.

dario (eng-runtime): main engineering constraints: database schema changes are incremental but we have a KV cache migration that can invalidate running processes. we have to avoid cold-cache thundering at switchover. suggestion: rolling upgrade with dual-read cache layer for one minor release.

rachel (solutions): +1 on rolling. For customer B netops require a deterministic handshake: service advertises a short-lived cert that their firewall can validate, then we open new control plane route. they also want the upgrade to provide a clear revert step they can run without support.

jess (pm-customer): their security team also requested KMS integration checklists and examples for HSM-backed keys. plus a tiny runbook snippet they can hand to netops.

ben (infra): operationally we can provide a three-step network handshake: 1) customer adds allowlist IPs, 2) deploy exposes handshake endpoint, 3) customer issues TLS pinning via our CSR flow. we need automation for step 1->3 to make it low-touch.

maya (product): action items we need for M1/launch: bundle of docs + sample scripts, an automated handshake CLI, upgrade modal that warns about cache warm-up, and a clear rollback command. estimate?

dario (eng-runtime): eng estimate: CLI + server-side handshake endpoint ~2w, cache dual-read support + rollout flags ~3w, rollback scripting + tests ~1w. that's ~6w with one eng. parallelize with infra for cert flow.

ben (infra): infra work: KMS/HSM integration guide + config templates ~1w, allowlist automation + sample cloud firewall rules 3d, testing harness for network flaps 4d.

rachel (solutions): I'll draft the customer-facing runbook and checklist. need sample commands. can we provide a small script we can paste into their change window?

maya (product): yes. prioritize script + checklist and handshake CLI as M1. full blue/green with operator UI as M2.

jess (pm-customer): can we include a preflight validator? netops insist on a dry-run that validates ports, certs, and KMS access without changing state.

dario (eng-runtime): doable — will add a `--dry-run` to the handshake CLI and a `validate-preflight` endpoint. small note: preflight will need temporary token scopes; document expiry and least-priv rules.

ben (infra): also want a small metrics and log hook we can expose during upgrade so customers can confirm no token errors. export path: /metrics/upgrade_lifecycle.

deploy-bot: deployment scheduled: private-handshake-cli v0.1.0 -> staging at 2025-08-12T03:00:00Z (rolling). :rocket:

maya (product): perfect. I'll write the PRD fragment and M1 acceptance criteria:
- handshake CLI with --dry-run and automated CSR flow
- runbook + sample firewall rules and allowlist automation
- dual-read cache mode with rollout flag and documented warm-up behavior
- rollback command that reverses control-plane routes and cache flag
- preflight validator and /metrics/upgrade_lifecycle endpoint

maya (product): any blockers?

dario (eng-runtime): need owner for QA tests and a staging customer to run the flow. also need time window for simulating network partitions.

rachel (solutions): I can coordinate a partner sandbox and run QA with them.

ben (infra): I'll own KMS doc + metrics hook.

maya (product): ok assigning: dario (eng) owner of CLI & dual-read changes, ben infra owner for KMS+metrics, rachel owner for runbook + staging test, jess to coordinate customer comms. timeframe target 6 weeks for M1.

maya (product): thanks — will drop this into the roadmap board and ping again for status updates. :thumbsup:
